title: Grateful Dead Live at Soldier's And Sailors Memorial Hall on 1972-11-13

ai_review.summary: Top‑tier 1972 audience tape captures an incendiary Dark Star > Morning Dew stretch with blazing energy and solid overall performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality Bear audience tape – deep, clear and surprisingly clean for the era despite some hiss. Musically the show shines around the massive Dark Star → Morning Dew sequence, backed by an intense Playing in the Band jam and a fiery Promised Land opener, while only a few numbers like Sugar Magnolia feel a bit sloppy.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews consistently praise the show’s energy and standout Dark Star/Dew, while noting the audience tape is top‑tier for ’72; average star rating is 4.4, so a 4.3 overall reflects strong musical performance plus excellent recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Bear’s audience tape is deep and clear with good balance; some hiss noted but overall considered top‑tier for a 1972 AUD, no major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set builds strong momentum, highlighted by a massive Dark Star → Morning Dew pairing; the jam sections flow well despite missing portions of Set 1.

band_member_comments.Phil: Outstanding bass solo and stomping bass lines are repeatedly praised, especially during the Dark Star climax.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (keys) is noted for leading the transition out of the dark jam into a less ominous feel.
